A simple timeline from left to right showing the progression of Nigerian Constitutions: 1914 (Lugard's Council) -> 1922 (Clifford) -> 1946 (Richards) -> 1951 (Macpherson) -> 1954 (Lyttelton) -> 1960 (Independence). Below 1922, a small icon of a ballot box with the text "Elective Principle (Lagos & Calabar)".

A three-column chart showing the Division of Legislative Powers under the 1954 Constitution. Column 1: "Exclusive List (Federal Only)" with icons for a soldier (Defence) and a coin (Currency). Column 2: "Concurrent List (Federal & Regional)" with icons for a graduation cap (Higher Education) and a factory (Industry). Column 3: "Residual List (Regional Only)" with icons for local chiefs (Chieftaincy) and a market (Local trade).
A map of Nigeria divided into three bold distinct sections: Northern Region (largest, top), Western Region (bottom left), and Eastern Region (bottom right). The boundaries should be clear.
